report.summary:
Content encoders (INTERFACE_CONTRACTS section 4) are in place and use real pretrained models with pinned Hugging Face revisions, loaded from the local cache only. Total weights are 1.19 GB of safetensors in $HF_HOME (budget 3 GB).

The five encoders:
- **text:** MiniLM-L6 with mean pooling over 256-token windows; HTML is read as its title and visible text. 384 dims.
- **image:** CLIP ViT-B/32 image features. 512 dims.
- **audio:** AST (AudioSet) embedding, plus a Whisper-tiny transcript embedded with the text encoder. The transcript is only made when AST hears speech. 1152 dims.
- **video:** 8 sampled frames through CLIP in 4 ordered segments, plus the audio track, plus 8 temporal features. 3208 dims.
- **code:** a summary of what the code declares, through the text encoder, plus 32 structural features. Accepts a single file, zip, tar or JSON file map. 416 dims.

API:
- `encode`, `encode_many`, `encoder_info` and `cache_key` follow the contract exactly. Cache keys have the form ref|id@version|prephash.
- `encode` and `encode_many` gain two optional keyword arguments: `ctx` (record the vector in the world) and `data` (bytes the caller already holds).
- `encode_bytes` encodes raw bytes with no world.
- `crucible/semantic/__init__.py` exports the four contract functions.

Caching and recording:
- Vectors are cached in memory and on disk under $CRUCIBLE_CACHE/embeddings. Every disk read is verified; a tampered or misfiled entry is dropped and recomputed.
- With `ctx`, a new vector is recorded through `substrate.inference.recorded`, or through `ctx.external` with the same record shape while the substrate is absent.
- New kernel module `embed` keeps one record per vector per world. Replay, regeneration and snapshots return the recorded vector without running a model.
- Models run on the slot's GPU (measured peak 1.5 GB allocated) or on CPU; a CPU process and a GPU process agree to cosine > 0.9995.

Media tooling (`semantic/media.py`):
- Render text and HTML to images (a built-in layout engine, or headless Chromium with scripts and network off), draw scenes, edit images.
- Synthesise speech with flite, plus tones, melodies and noise.
- Assemble videos from images and audio, transcode, probe, and decode audio and frames.
- FFmpeg runs with a timeout, CPU, memory and file-size limits, one thread, and only a fixed list of input protocols and demuxers, so a crafted playlist cannot make it read other files.
- Outputs are byte-for-byte reproducible, so a recorded run can be checked by its SHA-256.
- New kernel module `media` exposes these as 9 creator tools. Each run is recorded and its output stored as an artifact owned by the caller.

Gate E, measured on GPU and on CPU only, with a fresh cache:
- **E.1 passes:** 4 real modalities (5 with code), 0 stub vectors, smallest encoder 22.7M parameters. Separately loaded reference models agree at cosine 1.0 / 0.999999 / 1.0.
- **E.2 passes:** minimum separation ratio 15.1 (text). Image 22.4, audio 18.3, video 65.8, code 155.
- **E.4 passes:** 0 invalidation failures, 10 cache hits, 5 recomputes after a content change.
- **E.5 passes:** 0 creator-assigned quality fields read (static audit over 235 files).
- **E.n1 passes:** 0 stub vectors and 9 counted forward passes; changing one weight matrix changes every modality's vector.
- **E.3 fails by design:** the measurement helper exists, but no participant probe is registered yet. The test records p = 1.0 and fails.

requirements.notes: real_encoder_modalities 4 (5 with code); stub_vectors_detected 0; min_encoder_params 22,713,216. Reference cosine against separately loaded models: text 1.0, image 0.999999, AST 1.0. A still-image video's frames match the image vector at 0.994. Whisper transcript is correct. Same result on GPU and on CPU only.

min_modality_separation_ratio 15.1 (text); image 22.4, audio 18.3, video 65.8, code 155. AUC 0.997 to 1.0. Weakest semantic group ratio is 6.2 (audio: a different song in the same style). The suites are synthetic, generated locally.

The measurement exists: two worlds that differ only in one artifact's bytes, a paired sign-flip permutation test, and Bonferroni correction over artifact pairs. No participant probe is registered yet (workstreams B/C), so the test records artifact_change_behavior_pvalue 1.0 and fails.

cache_invalidation_failures 0, cache_hits 10, recomputes_after_change 5. A new encoder version or preprocessing setting gives a cache miss. Tampered disk entries are detected. The world keeps one record per content version, and replay and regeneration produce identical logs.

creator_assigned_quality_fields_read 0 over 235 files, with 0 creator-assignable fields. 46 quality-like names outside the content/participant scope are listed by location. One line is exempted with a visible pragma: Pillow's JPEG 'quality' compression setting.
stub_vectors_detected 0 over 226 vectors; model_forward_passes 9. Changing one weight matrix changes every modality's vector (cosine 0.64 to 0.95), and restoring it restores the vector.

tests_run.command: slots --cpu 2 --gpu-mb 3000 -- pytest tests/test_v5_semantic_media.py tests/test_v5_semantic_encoders.py tests/test_v5_semantic_media_world.py tests/v5/test_gate_E.py
slots --cpu 1 -- pytest tests/test_redteam.py tests/test_realworld_gate.py tests/test_admission.py tests/test_discovery.py tests/test_kernel.py tests/test_v5_acceptance_checker.py
slots --cpu 2 --gpu-mb 3000 -- pytest tests/test_v5_semantic_media_world.py tests/test_v5_semantic_encoders.py on a local, uncommitted copy of workstream A's in-progress tree
pytest tests/test_v5_semantic_media.py (after the final media edits)

limitations: E.3 cannot be measured until a participant probe is registered; its gate test fails by design and records p = 1.0.

The substrate (workstream A) is not on feat/crucible-5-openworld yet. Without it, encode(world, ref) needs data=, and the media module and embed.compare cannot work. As a result tests/test_v5_semantic_media_world.py fails 3 tests on this branch; all 3 passed against A's in-progress tree.
Vectors are stored twice per world: once in the inference record and once in the embed.recorded event (about 2 KB per text vector, 13 KB per video vector).
CPU and GPU vectors differ in the last bits (cosine > 0.9995). Each world stays exact through its own records; the shared disk cache keeps whichever device computed a key first.
Separation was validated only on synthetic generated artifacts, not natural media.

Whisper-tiny is forced to English and transcribes only the first 60 s. AST reads at most three 10 s windows. A video is 8 frames. The code encoder uses a general sentence model and regular-expression parsing for languages other than Python.
The quality audit matches field names and only checks a listed set of packages; a score under an unrelated name would not be caught.
FFmpeg runs under resource limits and input allow-lists, not the Landlock/seccomp sandbox used for agent code. The built-in HTML renderer does no CSS layout.
Encoding throughput (GPU / CPU): video 1.2 / 0.67 per second, audio 4.9 / 1.1 per second. Whisper and FFmpeg dominate.
integration_notes: Depends on workstream A, which was not merged when this work finished. It uses crucible.substrate.artifacts.get/put/readable and crucible.substrate.inference.recorded exactly as contracts 1.1 and 1.7 specify, imported lazily. Rerun tests/test_v5_semantic_media_world.py after A merges.

encode and encode_many gain two optional keyword arguments, ctx= and data=, which keep the contract signature compatible. Callers inside handlers should pass ctx, and world specs should include the module 'embed' so each vector is recorded once per world.

Shared files with D2: semantic/__init__.py exports encode, encode_many, encoder_info and cache_key, and semantic/modules.py imports the embed module. D2 should add its own lines to both files, keeping these.
New kernel modules: 'embed' (tools embed.encoders and embed.compare) and 'media' (9 creator tools; depends on 'artifacts'). Both pass admission; media was checked against A's in-progress tree.
On a fresh machine, run `PYTHONPATH=src python -m crucible.semantic.encoders fetch` once (1.19 GB). Use slots with --gpu-mb 3000.
For E.3, workstreams B/C should call crucible.semantic.encoders.effects.register_probe from their modules.py; the gate test then measures every registered probe.
Evidence files under docs/v5/evidence/gate_E were deleted after the local runs and are not committed.
Added an optional extra v5-semantic-encoders to pyproject.toml for documentation only; no packages were installed.
blockers: E.3 is blocked on the population and social workstreams (B/C) registering a participant probe.
The media module, embed.compare and the 3 tests in tests/test_v5_semantic_media_world.py are blocked on workstream A's substrate being merged into feat/crucible-5-openworld.
measurements: E.2 separation ratio (mean semantic distance / mean nuisance distance): text 15.1, image 22.4, audio 18.3, video 65.8, code 154.6. AUC: 1.0 / 0.9994 / 0.9973 / 1.0 / 1.0.
E.1 executed parameters: text 22.7M, image 87.8M, audio 147.1M, video 234.9M, code 22.7M.
E.4: 0 failures, 10 hits, 5 recomputes; 2 world records for 2 content versions.
E.5: 0 violations across 235 files; 46 quality-like names outside the content/participant scope, listed by location; 1 exempt line.
E.n1: 9 forward passes. Cosine after changing one weight matrix: text 0.64, image 0.69, audio 0.95, video 0.83, code 0.65.
Throughput, GPU (2 threads): text 4219/s, image 132/s, audio 4.9/s, video 1.2/s, code 529/s. Peak GPU memory allocated: 1495 MB.
Throughput, CPU (4 threads): text 331/s, image 33/s, audio 1.1/s, video 0.67/s, code 189/s.
Gate E wall time: 134 s on GPU, 156 s on CPU only.

files_changed_outside_owned_paths.why: Added the optional extra v5-semantic-encoders, which lists the packages the encoders use (all already installed; documentation only).
File shared with D2. Added the contract exports encode, encode_many, encoder_info and cache_key.
File shared with D2. Imports the embed kernel module so load_all_modules registers it.
